programs.rightsClaimSummary: Acadia's July 13 2023 SEC Form 8-K states Neuren granted it a worldwide exclusive trofinetide development and commercial license for all indications. Its 2026 Form 10-Q reports continuing DAYBUE commercialization. The license's detailed continuing obligations or independent legal enforceability have not been adjudicated.

sourceDocuments.assertion: July 13 2023 8-K describes amended and restated global exclusive Neuren licensing of trofinetide, for all indications, and attendant commercial arrangements.
2026 Q2 10-Q documents ongoing commercial DAYBUE trofinetide for FDA-approved Rett syndrome, originally approved March 10 2023; no 2026 pending FDA PDUFA for these historic studies.
Licensor Neuren states Acadia holds a worldwide exclusive trofinetide license; also notes the March 2023 prior FDA approval.
Acadia-sponsored trofinetide Rett syndrome open-label extension LILAC-2; sponsor terminated after commercial approval to switch patients to commercial product.
Acadia-sponsored trofinetide Rett syndrome DAFFODIL study in girls 2-5; sponsor terminated after FDA marketing approval and redirected patients to commercial trofinetide.

ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04181723 records Acadia-sponsored pivotal LAVENDER randomized trofinetide Phase 3 trial in Rett syndrome; historical study associated with existing FDA-approved DAYBUE, not a new 2026 PDUFA.
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04279314 records Acadia-sponsored long-term open-label LILAC trofinetide extension in Rett syndrome; completed historical safety work.
Acadia announced European Commission authorization for trofinetide (DAYBU) in August 2026; this is a completed EU action and not a pending U.S. FDA PDUFA date.

trialLinks.indication: Rett syndrome; long-term open-label trofinetide treatment
Rett syndrome in girls aged 2-5 years; trofinetide long-term safety
Rett syndrome in girls and women; trofinetide efficacy trial supporting existing commercial DAYBUE
Rett syndrome; open-label trofinetide safety extension

programs.rightsClaimSummary: Iovance 2026 Q2 SEC report discloses NIH TIL patent licensing with exclusive, co-exclusive and non-exclusive elements and NCI collaboration. Its TILVANCE-301 registrational study investigates lifileucel with pembrolizumab in untreated advanced melanoma. Prior AMTAGVI approval is for previously treated melanoma and does not approve this frontline combination.

sourceDocuments.assertion: June 2026 Iovance 10-Q describes NIH/NCI TIL IP licenses, milestone and royalty liabilities, termination terms, and the ongoing TILVANCE-301 frontline advanced melanoma lifileucel+ pembrolizumab confirmatory Phase 3 study.
Iovance lists TILVANCE-301 as Phase 3 lifileucel+pembrolizumab frontline melanoma trial, with separate lung and sarcoma programs.
Company's TILVANCE-301 detail page directly identifies NCT05727904 and compares lifileucel+pembrolizumab against pembrolizumab alone.
NCI identifies NCT05727904, IOV-MEL-301 and TILVANCE-301 together; current investigational combination is not an established new FDA action date.
NCT05727904 is a Phase 3 melanoma lifileucel plus pembrolizumab comparison trial sponsored by Iovance.

trialLinks.indication: Untreated unresectable or metastatic melanoma, lifileucel plus pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab alone
